done_when: A follow-up that names a period answers for that period whatever window the model emits; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: When `parseTimeWindow` cannot resolve the wording, line 389 preserves any model-emitted window merely because the question contains a period word. For example, with a prior July 2026 answer, “What about August?” parses to null; if the model emits September, the service answers September, and if it emits no window, the service inherits July. The added test at line 592 only supplies the correct August model window, so it cannot catch this. The same heuristic treats granularity requests such as “Show Actual by month” as naming a period, allowing an invented model window instead of aggregating or inheriting. This violates the required behavior regardless of the model output.
findings.title: Not done: Named periods must override the model; no-period questions must inherit or aggregate; edited periods must rerun as chosen

findings.body: All added regression scenarios invoke `ChatService.ask` with fake model, executor, and warehouse boundaries. They do not exercise the user-facing path through a browser, running API, real database, prior-turn transport, and period-control interaction. Repository discovery found only Vitest/jsdom frontend tests with a mocked API and backend unit tests, not a Playwright flow covering explicit-period override, no-period inheritance/aggregation, and changing an answer’s period. The required end-to-end proof therefore remains missing.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
